paper.title: Algorithm 322: F-Distribution [S14]
paper.venue: Communications of the ACM 11(2), 116-117 (CALGO/TOMS Algorithm 322; Field 1969 and Tolman 1979 remarks)
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/322.gz (the ACM article was not read; the shipped archive contains the Fortran 77 coding and the test program cited here)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 322.gz (downloaded 2026-11-27, sha256 f90c21567ea61d9ad8fdc0b9faaf799f9f467417ed71b04852e445b8eb294ecd); uncompressed text sha256 c6b619e2b6e13d810f8bff0b576f14ddce6d82dc9f2c0904885ea5c75ddee03b
code.note: Plain text after gunzip. Contains the Fortran 77 FUNCTION PROB(LM,LN,X) (Larry Weissman's recoding, 28-Mar-94), the PROGRAM tstprob test driver, and a shar archive with a C version (fisher.c). Use the Fortran only. Expect gfortran -std=legacy; the driver writes to stdout. Test only the F-distribution rows of the driver, because the claim is about the F tables.

claim.location: The test program PROGRAM tstprob in the uncompressed 322.txt, the F-distribution block of the DATA statements: the critical values f(i) (lines 178-200) with their expected upper-tail probabilities pf(i) (line 210, the 0.05 block is entries 51-75). Registered: two critical values from that block. The driver computes p = 1 - PROB(nf1, nf2, f) and prints it beside the expected pf. Entry 61-65 is the 3rd row (nf1=10) of the 0.05 block, and the 3rd column of that row is nf2=10 (f(63)=2.9782, line 192). Entry 51 is nf1=1, nf2=1 (f=161.45, line 190, 'A 161.45' in the 0.05 block).
claim.metric: The upper-tail probability p = 1 - PROB(M, N, X) for the F-ratio X with numerator df M and denominator df N, compared with the expected probability in the shipped DATA table (0.05 for both points).
claim.paper_value: Shipped test driver expected values: P(F(1,1) > 161.45) = 0.05 and P(F(10,10) > 2.9782) = 0.05 (the printed pf DATA entries, not a value read from the CACM article).

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The shipped expected values are printed to three decimals (0.050). The table critical values are given to 4-5 significant digits, and their rounding moves the exact tail probability by about 1e-5 at these points, so a correct rebuild should agree to well within 5e-4. The tolerance is 1% of the 0.05 level: loose enough for single precision (REAL) arithmetic and the algorithm's own series truncation, tight enough to fail a wrong tail or a wrong df order. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute (two evaluations of the series at most).
cost.data_size: None; the test values are in the driver's DATA statements.
cost.data_licence: No data. Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence of the archive; the rerun should record the licence it finds in the archive.

why: A 1968 statistical algorithm ships its own table of critical values and expected tail probabilities. The probability needs the whole incomplete-beta-type series in PROB, so a correct rebuild must compute it; a closed form for the tail does not exist at these df.
